title: pi-assert configuration
description: Schema for .pi/asserts.json — shell-assertion guard configuration for pi.

$schema.description: JSON Schema reference for editor autocompletion and validation.

local.description: User-defined assertions and presets. Removable via the /asserts UI.

oneOf.description: A shell-based assert: `shell` (and optional `filter`/`when`) run on a hook.

description.description: Human-readable description of what this assert guards. Required.

hook.description: Supported native or synthetic hook. Tool failures block or patch; turn_end and agent_settled failures report only; agent_end failures request one corrective turn; session_before_switch and session_before_fork failures cancel the action. assert_result handles individual assertion decisions and is always report-only. session_shutdown is intentionally unsupported because Pi does not expose cancellation for it.

filter.description: Filter matched against the hook adapter's bounded candidate: { ...event.input, toolName } for tool hooks; otherwise { event, ...documented scalar metadata }. Every key is required to match (implicit AND); omitted or empty filters match every candidate. Dot-separated keys resolve nested candidate fields. Every string value is normally a JavaScript regular-expression source tested with RegExp.test() against a string candidate; use anchors such as '^bash$' for exact matching. Invalid regexes fail runtime configuration loading. Numbers, booleans, and null use strict equality without coercion. Arrays are any-of and apply the same rule to each member; an empty array matches nothing. assert_result narrows this contract: assertionRef/runId/event are regex sources, outcome is an exact enum value, and code is numeric or null.

anyOf.description: JavaScript regular-expression source. It is unanchored unless ^ and $ are included; no regex-literal delimiters or flags are supported.
Non-string scalar matched with strict equality and no type coercion.
Any-of array. String members are JavaScript regex sources; number, boolean, and null members use strict equality. An empty array matches nothing.
JavaScript regular-expression source tested against string candidates.

shell.description: Shell command whose exit code decides pass/fail. Exit 0 passes; non-zero applies the selected hook's block, patch, cancel, or report policy. Pipes, redirects, &&, || all work.

when.description: Optional precondition shell command. The main shell only runs when this exits 0. Use for dynamic runtime conditions (dirty git state, file existence, etc.) that filter cannot express.

default.description: If true, this assert is active by default for new sessions. Defaults to false.

preset.description: Mutual exclusivity: a shell assert must not carry `preset` (use a preset entry instead).

oneOf.description: A preset: a named bundle of `source/name` refs expanded by activeList(). Presets and shell asserts are mutually exclusive.

description.description: Human-readable description of what this preset guards. Required.

preset.description: Qualified "source/name" refs (local/name or owner/repo/name) expanded to their shell asserts when the preset is active. Empty array is valid. Ref shape is enforced at write time by validatePresetShape (REF_RE).

default.description: If true, this preset is active by default for new sessions (activating the preset, not its members' own defaults). Defaults to false.

shell.description: Mutual exclusivity: a preset must not carry `shell`.

hook.description: Mutual exclusivity: a preset must not carry `hook`.

assertResultFilter.description: Bounded assert_result filter. assertionRef, runId, and event use regex matching; outcome is exact any-of; code uses strict numeric/null matching.

repo.description: Asserts installed from a specific repository (keyed by owner/repo). Removable via the /asserts UI.
